question: Should OpenClaw add a generic action-aware tool-policy contract for multiplexed tools, and what trusted bypass semantics should approved workflows use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix defines public config grammar and a security boundary across message sends, gateway writes, sender policy, sandbox policy, and tool invocation paths.

options.title: Design Generic Action Policy
options.body: Add a typed action-aware policy grammar with documented precedence, wildcard behavior, and trusted-context tests for message and gateway actions.

options.title: Narrow To Message And Gateway
options.body: Add separate controls for the current `message` and `gateway` cases, reducing immediate scope but creating parallel policy surfaces that may drift.

options.title: Defer To Confirmation Gate
options.body: Use the adjacent confirmation-gate direction for human approval and accept that static least-privilege action deny remains unavailable for now.

recommendation.title: Design Generic Action Policy
recommendation.body: Add a typed action-aware policy grammar with documented precedence, wildcard behavior, and trusted-context tests for message and gateway actions.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest routing candidate from live review discussion plus current policy/message/gateway file history.
